newsitem.title: PERU: Talks hinge on Peru addressing main demand -rebels.
newsitem.headline: Talks hinge on Peru addressing main demand -rebels.

text.p: The go-ahead for peace talks between Peru and Marxist rebels holding 73 captives hinged on Sunday on whether the government would agree to discuss the hostage takers' demand for the release of jailed comrades.

Both sides have said they are ready to meet face-to-face but the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) claimed on Saturday the government was blocking negotiations by refusing to consider their main demand.

"There is no possibility of starting conversations because in practice they are asking us beforehand to drop our request, which signifies a formal call to surrender which we will never accept," an MRTA spokesman said on Saturday from within the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence.

Within a framework of discussing all issues, including the main demand to free some 400 jailed rebels, "we are ready to converse as we were willing to since we occupied this diplomatic site," the spokesman, assumed to be MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, said via two-way radio.

In a five-point communique that showed the two sides edging towards the talks, the MRTA accepted the government's proposal of former hostage and Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent on a "guarantor" commission overseeing the talks.
"The government proposal to include a representative from Canada is acceptable," said Cerpa. He had already agreed to the Red Cross and the Vatican as members of the commission.
Government negotiator Domingo Palermo announced on Friday Vincent would sit on the commission, but ruled out considering the release of MRTA prisoners.
However, President Alberto Fujimori has hinted the demand could be adressed in talks to end the the 32-day siege.
"It is likely to come up as a theme in the negotiations, but the Peruvian government will not agree to a release," Fujimori said in an interview with Japan's television NHK.

Tokyo's task force in Lima cautiously welcomed the MRTA communique as at least focusing the precise point of dispute and recognising a need for private rather than public negotiations. "The distance is becoming smaller," a task force official said.
But it was not known if the rebels had agreed to the government's proposal of holding the meeting in a building outside the residence.

"A meeting has to be within the residence," Isaac Velazco, the MRTA's international spokesman, told Reuters by telephone from Copenhagen. Cerpa did not say whether he was willing to leave the diplomatic mansion for the talks.

Police further tightened security on Sunday around the residence. Replacing national policemen with special force officers, they increased the number of personnel on guard where hundreds of journalists are camped out behind security cordons a distance of two city blocks on all four sides.

Closer to the compound, witnesses noted unusual movement of security officers in the early hours on Sunday. About 10 special police officers passed in front of the residence's main entrance just before 1 a.m. (0600 GMT), they said.
Cerpa has said previous threatening manoeuvres where police approached the residence had provoked rebels to fire shots into the air from within the booby-trapped and mined compound.

Adding to the tension, a shot heard in the distance sent journalists scurrying in different directions. But the nervy calm returned as policemen were unmoved, saying the sound came from several blocks away.
A shootout within earshot of the residence between police and criminals also caused brief panic at the site on Saturday.
Police evicted on Saturday six journalists from the roof of a building near the besieged residence.

Five photographers and a television cameraman, mostly from international news agencies, were ordered down from the vantage point they had manned in shifts, hauling up food by rope, since the siege began.
The order was signed by police Gen. Fernando Gamero Febres and obliged the journalists to come down "for strict reasons of security". The eviction took place without incident.
